claims.text: The framework separately calculates lattice and electronic thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice thermal conductivity is calculated using Green–Kubo molecular dynamics with on-the-fly machine-learned force fields.
Electronic transport is calculated from DFT electronic structure and Boltzmann transport using deformation-potential relaxation times and spin–orbit coupling.
The framework will be more accurate than conventional models that conflate lattice and electronic heat transport.
The predicted total thermal conductivity will be within ±15% of experiment.
The framework will improve predictive accuracy by 30–50% relative to earlier approaches.
The target material is defect-free bulk HfNbTaTiZr with controlled oxygen below 1 wt.%.
Atomic-scale mass and force-constant fluctuations dominate phonon scattering.
Electronic heat conduction is mediated by free carriers whose relaxation times are governed by deformation-potential effects.
Classical molecular dynamics can capture phonon dynamics at arbitrary order, including higher-order anharmonic effects.
Separating the phonon and electronic channels captures the dominant scattering mechanism in each channel and avoids averaging errors inherent to conflated models.
The summed conductivity will reproduce a high-temperature experimental benchmark of 10–17 W/(K m) within ±15%.
Traditional approaches that do not distinguish lattice and electronic contributions have errors of at least 25%.
The framework is applicable from 300 to 1200 K for samples with low defect and oxygen content.
Predictions are less reliable below 200 K because electron–phonon interactions pose additional challenges.
Inelastic neutron or X-ray scattering and electronic transport spectroscopy can separately determine the lattice and electronic conductivity contributions over 300–1200 K.
Deviation above ±15% for either contribution or their sum, or improvement below approximately 30%, is the stated falsification criterion.

contradictions.description: The design proposes experimental separation using neutron/X-ray scattering and electronic spectroscopy, but the listed 'measurements' describe Green–Kubo MD and DFT-Boltzmann calculations, which are predictions rather than experimental measurements.
